edit.description: `readQueueFiles` resolves the tip once and hands `readQueueAtRef` the sha, so that function's "the ref does not move" comment holds as written
`readFileAtRef`'s own `ls-tree`-then-`show` pair is the inner straddle; it and `listTreeBlobNames` compose at one resolved sha, per `revParse`
the harvest's tracked-at-HEAD probe — the other symbolic-`HEAD` read, one tip for every candidate, same log-and-continue class

summary: the queue read lists and shows at the symbolic HEAD, so a sibling's commit mid-read kills it; one read resolves one tip, at every src/ site composing HEAD: across git calls

per.section: Dispatch reads come from the tip, not the tree

acceptance: A queue read resolves its tip to a sha once and lists and shows at that sha, so a concurrent commit is the next read's and never half of this one; `readFileAtRef`'s own two legs run at one sha, and the friction harvest resolves once for all candidates, keeping its log-and-continue class. `pnpm tsc --noEmit` and the suite green.
tests: a queue read whose tip moves between the listing and the file reads returns the queue the listing's tip held
notes: Field-paid 2026-09-30, build wave refill: `show HEAD:<entry>` exited 1 (`fatal: path ... does not exist in 'HEAD'`) after `ls-tree HEAD` had listed it. Verified on disk this tick: the only symbolic-`HEAD` reads in `src/` are pendingLedger.ts:404 and friction.ts:311; every other `readFileAtRef`/`listTreeBlobNames` caller already hands a resolved sha (`ctx.commitSha`, `ctx.baseSha`, `span.head`). `revParse` (src/git.ts:123) is the resolver.
